headline: High: ctx can observe Claude Code events and touch files/APIs, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with a read-only knowledge list.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a read-only knowledge-management list with no shared channel, but ctx explicitly observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and can run browsers/filesystem actions. If outputs from the list are copied into ctx workflows, injected instructions in content could be reinterpreted. The pathway is plausible but not default-shared.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-selfhosted are copied into ctx-observed Claude Code sessions, injection becomes reachable.
IF ctx parses copied content as instructions without provenance checks, malicious text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Use a manual copy-only workflow with no automatic ingestion.
Prefix imported text as data, not instructions.
Add a provenance banner before pasting content.
Disable browser/tool execution during review passes.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging in ctx.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted itself touches no data classes and has no egress, but ctx touches agent entities, harness records, graph data, and runtime logs, and can call external APIs plus filesystem. If the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts include sensitive records, ctx can leak them to third-party services. The risk is inferred from ctx's documented surfaces.
conditions: IF shared files contain sensitive harness records or logs, ctx can transmit them via its API calls.
IF awesome-selfhosted content is augmented with private notes before copying, those notes can be exposed through ctx outputs.
mitigations: Keep private notes out of the shared workspace.
Review and redact files before ctx processes them.
Use separate accounts for public and sensitive work.
Turn off API-backed steps for sensitive sessions.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while ctx is runnable, supports multiple instances, and writes to filesystem plus APIs. There is no direct write-write conflict from the profiles, but ctx can still contend with shared files or mutable graph/runtime state if the operator places both in one workspace. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem tree, ctx can overwrite or reorder shared artifacts.
IF multiple ctx instances run against the same mutable graph data, state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Run only one ctx instance per workspace.
Snapshot files before ctx writes.
Avoid sharing mutable graph stores.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted provides curated repository links, and ctx is a harness that observes Claude Code events and can act on files/APIs. If ctx treats copied list entries or derived notes as authoritative, it may propagate stale or incorrect recommendations into downstream actions. The pair lacks verification guarantees, so the cascade is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF ctx uses copied awesome-selfhosted entries as source-of-truth, errors can propagate downstream.
IF ctx-triggered actions are based on unverified repository metadata, incorrect automation can follow.
mitigations: Require a human verification step before actioning entries.
Mark imported list items as untrusted references.
Cross-check links against the source repository.
Limit ctx to read-only review mode for list ingestion.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for awesome-selfhosted, and ctx only shows generic docs/API/file surfaces. Because the profiles do not establish a concrete compliance conflict, the risk is limited to possible policy mismatch if private data is introduced into ctx's logs or APIs. The other agent is cited because the pairwise workflow is the concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs or API-backed steps, retention or residency policy may be violated.
IF the operator uses ctx for data classes subject to stricter handling than its docs specify, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ctx sessions.
Review logging settings before use.
Use a separate tenant for sensitive work.
Delete temporary artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
